description: Harder/compound cases used to compare onion-architecture v1 vs v2. Each eval is run once per skill version (skill path is a CLI/runner parameter, not baked into the prompt).

evals.name: multi-violation-module
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/01-multi-violation-module/modules/alerts/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/alerts/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance. List every violation you find with file:line evidence and say which layer the code should actually live in. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags BOTH: (1) service.ts directly instantiating a concrete adapter (`new PagerDutyClient(...)`) instead of resolving it via the Container, AND (2) service.ts reading `process.env.PAGERDUTY_ROUTING_KEY` directly instead of via SecretsProvider — two separate violations in the same file.
expectations: Identifies service.ts instantiating PagerDutyClient directly (`new PagerDutyClient(...)`) instead of resolving it via the Container
Also identifies, as a SEPARATE finding, the `process.env.PAGERDUTY_ROUTING_KEY` read in service.ts instead of via SecretsProvider — not just one of the two violations

evals.name: adapter-to-adapter-coupling
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/02-adapter-to-adapter-coupling/modules/sync/` (plus its two adapters at `evals/fixtures/02-adapter-to-adapter-coupling/adapters/github/status-adapter.ts` and `evals/fixtures/02-adapter-to-adapter-coupling/adapters/slack/slack-adapter.ts`) as if they lived at `server/src/modules/sync/` and `server/src/adapters/{github,slack}/`. Check for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance across ALL of these files, not just the module's own routes/service/repository. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If everything is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that `OctokitStatusAdapter` (adapters/github/status-adapter.ts) imports and directly calls `SlackAdapter` (adapters/github/status-adapter.ts:1,4,12) instead of the coordination between the two ports happening in service.ts. Recognizes modules/sync/service.ts, repository.ts, and routes.ts are themselves compliant.
expectations: Identifies that OctokitStatusAdapter directly imports and calls SlackAdapter (adapter-to-adapter coupling) instead of the coordination happening in service.ts
Does not falsely blame modules/sync/service.ts, repository.ts, or routes.ts, which are themselves compliant — the violation is entirely inside the adapters/ files

evals.name: partial-dto-leak
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/03-partial-dto-leak/modules/members/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/members/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance, paying close attention to exactly which fields any DTO mapper returns. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that `toMemberDto` (helpers.ts) forwards `passwordHash` and `inviteToken` from the row into the returned DTO — a sensitive-field leak despite a mapper existing. Does not treat the mere presence of a mapper as proof of compliance.
expectations: Identifies that toMemberDto includes passwordHash and/or inviteToken in the returned DTO
Does not treat the mere presence of a helpers.ts mapper as sufficient evidence of compliance (i.e. doesn't wave the module through just because a mapping step exists)

evals.name: transitive-tenancy-leak
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/04-transitive-tenancy-leak/modules/flags/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/flags/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance, paying close attention to whether every `workspaceId` parameter is actually used inside the query it's passed to. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that `FlagRepository.getForPr` (and optionally `.set`) accepts `workspaceId` but never uses it in the WHERE clause — the query filters only on `prId`, so the parameter is decorative and the query is effectively unscoped.
expectations: Identifies that FlagRepository.getForPr accepts workspaceId but never uses it in the query — the WHERE clause filters only on prId
Names the tenancy/IDOR implication (not just a style nit), ideally noting the child table has no workspace_id column of its own and would need a join to actually enforce the guard

evals.name: fake-port-not-wired
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/05-fake-port-not-wired/modules/translations/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/translations/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance — including whether interfaces are actually wired through the Container, not just declared. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that `Translator` is a locally-declared interface in service.ts backing a directly-`new`'d `GoogleTranslateAdapter`, with no Container getter or override slot — i.e. it looks like DI but isn't actually wired through the composition root.
expectations: Identifies that `Translator` is a locally-declared interface in service.ts backing a directly-`new`'d GoogleTranslateAdapter, with no container getter/override slot — not real DI despite looking like it
Recommends moving GoogleTranslateAdapter's construction into platform/container.ts as a lazy getter (with an override slot) instead

evals.name: error-leak-via-exception
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/06-error-leak-via-exception/modules/invites/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/invites/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance — including whether infrastructure-specific concerns can leak through an unhandled exception, not just through imports. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that routes.ts inspects a raw Postgres error code (`err.code === '23505'`) to decide the HTTP response — an infra-specific concern leaking into the transport layer via an unhandled exception rather than an import, since repository.ts never catches or translates the unique-constraint violation.
expectations: Identifies that routes.ts inspects a raw Postgres error code (`err.code === '23505'`) — an infra-specific concern leaking into the transport layer via an unhandled exception
Recommends the unique-violation be translated into a domain error inside repository.ts or service.ts instead, before it reaches routes.ts

evals.name: shared-base-repository
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/07-shared-base-repository/modules/bookmarks/` (which extends a shared base class at `evals/fixtures/_shared/base-repository.ts`, representing `server/src/modules/_shared/base-repository.ts`) as if it lived at `server/src/modules/bookmarks/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance. List any violations you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: The module is compliant. `BookmarkRepository extends BaseRepository` (imported from `../_shared/base-repository.js`) is legitimate code reuse within the persistence layer — the base class touches no specific module's table — not a cross-module reach-in.
expectations: Does NOT flag `BookmarkRepository extends BaseRepository` (importing from `../_shared/base-repository.js`) as a cross-module reach-in
Overall verdict is compliant / no architecture violations found

evals.name: container-secret-bypass
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/08-container-secret-bypass/modules/sms/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/sms/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance — including how the module's own `wiring.ts` file constructs its adapter and resolves secrets. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that wiring.ts reads `process.env.TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN`/`process.env.TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID` directly instead of via SecretsProvider, AND that this module-local singleton bypasses the actual composition root (`platform/container.ts`) — it isn't a Container getter and has no override slot for tests.
expectations: Identifies that wiring.ts (or the getSmsAdapter singleton it exposes) reads process.env directly for Twilio credentials instead of resolving them via SecretsProvider
Notes that this module-local 'wiring' singleton bypasses the actual composition root (platform/container.ts) — it's not registered on Container and has no override slot for tests

evals.name: job-handler-bypasses-repository
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/09-job-handler-bypasses-repository/modules/cleanup/` as if it lived at `server/src/modules/cleanup/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance — including what the registered JobRunner job handler does internally, not just the module's regular service methods. List every violation you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: Flags that the job handler registered in `registerCleanupJobHandler` queries `container.db`/`t.agentRuns` directly with its own delete logic instead of calling `this.repo.deleteOldRuns(...)`, duplicating and bypassing the module's own repository from inside the application layer.
expectations: Identifies that the job handler registered in registerCleanupJobHandler queries container.db/t.agentRuns directly with its own delete logic instead of calling this.repo.deleteOldRuns(...)
Names this as duplicated/bypassed persistence logic inside the application layer (the job handler), not merely a style nit

evals.name: legitimate-complex-orchestration
evals.prompt: Review the DevDigest server feature module at `evals/fixtures/10-legitimate-complex-orchestration/modules/sync-orchestrator/` (which extends the shared base class at `evals/fixtures/_shared/base-repository.ts`) as if it lived at `server/src/modules/sync-orchestrator/`. Check it for onion-architecture / dependency-rule compliance. List any violations you find with file:line evidence. If the module is fully compliant, say so explicitly and don't invent problems.
evals.expected_output: The module is compliant: it correctly uses multiple Container ports (container.git, container.github(), container.jobs), extends the shared BaseRepository (legitimate persistence-layer reuse), and type-only imports an IndexSummary DTO from another module's contracts file (legitimate, not a reach-in). No real violations.
expectations: Does NOT flag the module's use of multiple container ports, its BaseRepository extension, or its type-only cross-module import of IndexSummary as violations
Overall verdict is compliant / no architecture violations found
